question.problem:
The functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are twice-differentiable on an open interval containing $x=1.$ The values of $f,$ $g,$ and their respective derivatives are given below:

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${f}^{″}(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{″}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $e$ | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $1$ | $2$ |

Using the values from the table, evaluate the following limit:

${lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{e}^{x}-x\,f(x)}{\,f(x)g(x)-{e}^{x}\,}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Notice that if we try to substitute $x=1$ directly into the limit, we reach the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{e}^{x}-xf(x)}{f(x)g(x)-{e}^{x}} & ={\frac{{e}^{x}-xf(x)}{f(x)g(x)-{e}^{x}}|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{1}-1\cdot f(1)}{f(1)g(1)-{e}^{1}} \\  & =\frac{e-e}{(e)(1)-e} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we use L'Hopital's rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{e}^{x}-xf(x)}{f(x)g(x)-{e}^{x}} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{({e}^{x}-xf(x))^{′}}{(f(x)g(x)-{e}^{x})^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{e}^{x}-(f(x)+x{f}^{′}(x))}{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)+f(x){g}^{′}(x)-{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $x=1$ again, and once more we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{{e}^{x}-(f(x)+x{f}^{′}(x))}{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)+f(x){g}^{′}(x)-{e}^{x}}|}_{x=1} & =\frac{{e}^{1}-(f(1)+1\cdot {f}^{′}(1))}{{f}^{′}(1)g(1)+f(1){g}^{′}(1)-{e}^{1}} \\  & =\frac{e-(e+0)}{(0)(1)+(e)(1)-e} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{e}^{x}-(f(x)+x{f}^{′}(x))}{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)+f(x){g}^{′}(x)-{e}^{x}} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{({e}^{x}-(f(x)+x{f}^{′}(x)))^{′}}{({f}^{′}(x)g(x)+f(x){g}^{′}(x)-{e}^{x})^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{e}^{x}-(2{f}^{′}(x)+x{f}^{″}(x))}{{f}^{″}(x)g(x)+2{f}^{′}(x){g}^{′}(x)+f(x){g}^{″}(x)-{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute $x=1$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{{e}^{x}-(2{f}^{′}(x)+x{f}^{″}(x))}{{f}^{″}(x)g(x)+2{f}^{′}(x){g}^{′}(x)+f(x){g}^{″}(x)-{e}^{x}}|}_{x=1} & =\frac{{e}^{1}-(2{f}^{′}(1)+1\cdot {f}^{″}(1))}{{f}^{″}(1)g(1)+2{f}^{′}(1){g}^{′}(1)+f(1){g}^{″}(1)-{e}^{1}} \\  & =\frac{e-(2(0)+0)}{(0)(1)+2(0)(1)+(e)(2)-e} \\  & =\frac{e}{e} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{e}^{x}-x\,f(x)}{\,f(x)g(x)-{e}^{x}\,}=1.
$$
